name: A Small Terminal Cut Layer Must Be a Domino Wedge
statement: Let $K\subsetneq A$ be ample, put $D=A\setminus K$, and suppose every $d\in D$ is doubly blocked. If the residual graph on $D$ has a cut vertex and $|D|\le11$, then $|D|=11$ and its block-cut tree consists of two six-vertex dominoes sharing one articulation vertex. The articulation has degree two within each domino.
proof: The component-size theorem makes the residual graph connected, and double blocking excludes residual degree below two. Two leaf blocks then satisfy $|D|\ge|L_1|+|L_2|-1$, so one has at most six vertices. Bipartiteness and cube common-neighbor bounds leave only $C_4$, $C_6$, and the domino as possible two-connected induced-cube blocks. The degree-two carrier rules and an exhaustive symbolic passive-coordinate check exclude both cycles and a domino rooted at a degree-three vertex. Thus both leaf blocks are degree-two-rooted dominoes; together they already use eleven vertices, forcing equality and a common articulation.
